title: Human Anatomy II
mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the optic chiasm, which carries visual information to the brain for interpretation."
Just superior to the gland is the optic chiasm, which carries visual information to the brain for interpretation.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a disorder characterised by the hypersecretion of cortisol and androgens and possibly by excess aldosterone production."
Cushing syndrome is a disorder characterised by the hypersecretion of cortisol and androgens and possibly by excess aldosterone production.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the presence of excess ketone bodies in the blood.  Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS) consists of very elevated blood sugar levels."
Ketosis is the presence of excess ketone bodies in the blood.  Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS) consists of very elevated blood sugar levels.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a loss of bone matrix as parathyroid hormone increases to maintain blood levels of Ca2+ within their normal range."
The greatest risk is a loss of bone matrix as parathyroid hormone increases to maintain blood levels of Ca2+ within their normal range.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the major organ of excretion in the body, it is a paired organ located at the posterior aspect of the lumber region."
The kidney is the major organ of excretion in the body, it is a paired organ located at the posterior aspect of the lumber region.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the paired tube that convey the excreted urine from the kidney to the bladder."
The Ureter is the paired tube that convey the excreted urine from the kidney to the bladder.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a genetic disorder, not a hormonal disorder."
Achondroplasia is a genetic disorder, not a hormonal disorder.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a narrow membranous canal, about 4cm long, extending from the internal urethra orifice at the lower angle of the trigone of the bladder to the external urethra orifice."
The female urethra is a narrow membranous canal, about 4cm long, extending from the internal urethra orifice at the lower angle of the trigone of the bladder to the external urethra orifice.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an abnormally increased secretion of thyroid hormones."
Hyperthyroidism is an abnormally increased secretion of thyroid hormones.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is one of the largest endocrine glands, with a weight of approximately 20g."
The thyroid gland is one of the largest endocrine glands, with a weight of approximately 20g.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a collection of neurons in the hypothalamus that controls appetite."
The satiety center is a collection of neurons in the hypothalamus that controls appetite.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a chronic enlargement of the thyroid gland not due to a tumor."
Goiter is a chronic enlargement of the thyroid gland not due to a tumor.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a tube that exits the urinary bladder inferiorly and anteriorly."
The urethra is a tube that exits the urinary bladder inferiorly and anteriorly.
fib: ______ is the funnel-shaped commencement of the ureter.
Renal pelvis
The Renal pelvis is the funnel-shaped commencement of the ureter.
______ is a benign tumor; neuroblastoma is a malignant tumor.
Pheochromocytoma
Pheochromocytoma is a benign tumor; neuroblastoma is a malignant tumor.
______ is the second of the four volumes of Human Anatomy.
Human Anatomy (II)
Human Anatomy
II
Human Anatomy (II) is the second of the four volumes of Human Anatomy.
______ are those that are made of amino acids or proteins.
Non-steroid hormones
Non-steroid hormones are those that are made of amino acids or proteins.
______ can be defined as chemicals secreted by a cell that affect the functions of other cells.
Hormones
Hormones can be defined as chemicals secreted by a cell that affect the functions of other cells.
______ is composed of endocrine glands, which are ductless glands secreting chemical messengers into the circulatory system.
endocrine system
The endocrine system is composed of endocrine glands, which are ductless glands secreting chemical messengers into the circulatory system.
______ is the central portion of the gland and secretes epinephrine and norepinephrine.
adrenal medulla
The adrenal medulla is the central portion of the gland and secretes epinephrine and norepinephrine.
______ is a triangular area on the interior of the base of the bladder.
Trigone
Trigone is a triangular area on the interior of the base of the bladder.
______ is one of two major portal systems.
hypothalamohypophyseal portal system
The hypothalamohypophyseal portal system is one of two major portal systems.
______ is a complex organ made of specialised muscle layers and enervated by a reflex arc to the spine and central coordination in the brain.
urinary bladder
The urinary bladder is a complex organ made of specialised muscle layers and enervated by a reflex arc to the spine and central coordination in the brain.
______ is a 5 mm blind-ending tract which opens into eminence in the middle of the crest at the verumontanum.
prostatic utricle
The prostatic utricle is a 5 mm blind-ending tract which opens into eminence in the middle of the crest at the verumontanum.
______ is used for energy, stored as glycogen, or converted into fats.
Glucose
Glucose is used for energy, stored as glycogen, or converted into fats.
______ is a small, pinecone-shaped structure located superior and posterior to the thalamus of the brain.
pineal gland
The pineal gland is a small, pinecone-shaped structure located superior and posterior to the thalamus of the brain.
